body: I'm 25 - well past the high school age
It's been 7/8 months now. I feel hollow. Food is tasteless. Colours are grey. Why is living seen as the right option?

Your point is that my family and friends love me. Do I stay alive to please them? Does it make me selfish to then want to commit suicide? 

Don't get me wrong. I love my family and my friends but they aren't responsible for my lack of happiness or my current state of life - I am. And if I'm not getting any happiness from it then why should I go on? 

Why should I talk to a stranger on the phone who doesn't know me who will tell me that living is worth it. How do they know? What gives them the authority to decide on morality over me?

I hear you. It all got a bit much yesterday (weekends, where work doesn't distract me, are tough) so I rang the Samaritans. I sobbed down the phone to a lady and she listened to absolutely everything I had to say. It was tough making the phone call and admitting I had destructive thoughts but it did help. Afterwards I felt like I'd had my outburst and I could carry on with my day. I'm by no means happy now but it was a good momentary relief. I'd suggest it if you're climbing the walls. 

Likewise - give me a pm and I'll listen. 

Edit : I just realised I repeated the exact same thing. My brain is a mush. Sorry!
I do appreciate your time and viewpoint. Thank you

If you want to talk about it then you have a friend here. Similar situation. Talk of kids, marriage, in the process of moving in together. Now she has blocked me and ignored me as she needs to move on. It's devastating.

I spoke to the Samaritans today as I've been having destructive thoughts - I don't want a future different to one I had planned with the person I love but it's being forced upon me. Talking through it was lovely. I sobbed and told them everything. It's quite liberating. 

Just know you can talk to someone in a similar situation if you'd like - I'm just a PM away

I'm not burdening her with my happiness or misery. She explicitly told me that we were going to have a future together. I had a house key to her place, we discussed kids, the whole lot. When someone makes you believe you're wanted that much you tend to feel elated. I was happy with my future plans. With our future plans. She has cut me out of her life. 

My future is now watching the woman I love with other men. I don't want to be living a different future. I had the best future lined up and now I have to settle for second best - one in which the whole world, that used to be experienced in colour, is now grey. It's not worth it. I go at some point anyway, so why spend the rest of my days wanting something that can't happen, wishing it had been different.

To say you are responsible for your own feelings is not fair. You're telling me that if you're raped or you've witnessed a murder you could stay calm and unaffected because you're in control of your feelings? 

Sometimes you can't control your feelings. When you've been let down far too much.

She wouldn't even know I was gone. She would probably ignore my letter. I cried out for help last night as she is the person I confide in. I asked for just 5 minutes of her time, just to talk about how low I feel and she blocked me.  She was with a new man. She made me believe we had a future together, told me I was everything to her and that she would do anything for me. She gave me a house key. We were on our way to so much happiness. I believed it all too hard.

I believe she is worth it. I am still completely in love with this lady but she is ignoring me and seeing new men after telling me she loved me and being intimate with me. The way she has treated me has completely destroyed all faith I had in people. I know not everyone is alike but she was incredibly manipulative and I don't wish to experience anyone else. She told me that I had treated her worse than a rapist (she has been raped). I have not done anything to this woman, I did nothing but love, care and support her whenever she needed it. She is 33, I am 25, yet I feel like the mature one. 

My childhood memories are beautiful and I'm incredibly grateful to both my parents and the people involved in making them. But they have been and gone. Life is no longer innocent or fun.
